details: Escalating conflict between the U.S. and Iran near the Strait of Hormuz, including reported attacks on oil tankers, has pushed Brent crude oil futures above $100 a barrel on Wednesday, reaching their highest close since late May. This geopolitical instability is fueling global inflation concerns and increasing investor risk aversion, contributing to a downward trend in broader financial markets and implicitly impacting speculative assets like cryptocurrencies.
title: Middle East Tensions Drive Oil Prices Above $100, Pressuring Markets

details: The European Central Bank (ECB) raised its key interest rate by 25 basis points on Thursday, marking its second hike this year. This decision aims to combat persistent inflation, largely driven by surging energy costs exacerbated by the Middle East conflict. The ECB now forecasts inflation to remain above its 2% target until 2028, signaling a continued tight monetary policy stance in the Eurozone.
title: ECB Hikes Interest Rates Again Amid Persistent Inflationary Pressures

details: Robust U.S. Producer Price Index (PPI) data for August, showing a 0.4% rise for final demand, was released on Thursday. This stronger-than-expected inflation figure, coupled with rising oil prices, has significantly increased market expectations for a Federal Reserve interest rate hike next week, with odds now at 70%. Higher rates tend to reduce liquidity and investor appetite for riskier assets such as cryptocurrencies.
title: US Inflation Data Boosts Bets for Federal Reserve Rate Hike

details: The U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) announced the seizure of Telegram channels and cryptocurrency wallets, freezing over $52 million in cryptocurrency, connected to Xinbi Guarantee. This Chinese-language online marketplace allegedly facilitated services for scam centers targeting Americans, highlighting ongoing efforts by authorities to combat crypto-related fraud and money laundering.
title: US DOJ Freezes $52 Million in Crypto from China-Operated Scam Network
